The docs' "sandbox" pages cover flow-code execution isolation on self-hosted deployments ("Flow code (Code steps and piece actions) always runs inside a **sandbox**"), not an API test environment; the OpenAPI servers array lists only the production cloud host.
Per-release breaking-changes register covering API surface changes with upgrade guidance, plus dated changelogs; /v1 path versioning. No deprecation-window commitment.
Built-in FastAPI Swagger surface on a running self-hosted instance, gated behind ENV=dev; declared "an experimental setup". A self-hosted built-in rather than a vendor-hosted downloadable spec.
Per-service "Swagger Documentation Links" to the built-in interactive Swagger UI on the integrator's own instance, available only with ENV=dev; no vendor-hosted runnable playground.
Every "sandbox" hit is Open Terminal code-execution isolation or marketing copy; API keys come from the live instance and no test environment exists.

Keep-a-Changelog repository changelog with a SemVer commitment and per-version plugin-API migration guides. The REST reference is declared experimental and the :main container tag "can include breaking changes without warning".

Zero openapi/swagger/postman across the RESTful and legacy API docs; copyable XML/JSON request examples only. api.dynadot.com is a soft-200 host (identical "Page Not Found" body on any path), so absence was verified in page content.
Copyable request/response examples only; zero runner markers (try-it/playground/console) across the API documentation.

Dedicated API Sandbox on its own host (https://api-sandbox.dynadot.com) with separate keys and an account pre-funded with 10,000 in all supported currencies; some commands unavailable or differ in the sandbox (per-command labels).

URL-based major versioning (v2.0.0), SemVer statement, back-compat statement, and a Change Log History section; material caveat carried verbatim: the RESTful API documentation is Beta and "backward compatibility is not guaranteed".

OpenAPI 3.0.3 document for the MCP directory API, advertised from llms.txt and discoverable through an RFC 9727 API catalog at /.well-known/api-catalog (second row glama-api-catalog-20261106). Scope: directory API only; the Gateway is an MCP-protocol proxy.
Vendor-hosted reference with a per-endpoint "Try it" panel ("Requests are sent directly from this browser. Credentials are never stored."); client-side runner against the production API.

Hosted no-login MCP Inspector for testing remote MCP servers interactively. Scope carried in the excerpt: it tests arbitrary third-party servers; it is not an isolated sandbox of Glama's own directory API (glama.ai/changelog is 404; no test keys).

/v1 path versioning with a deprecation banner on the endpoint page and the matching machine-readable "deprecated": true flag in the OpenAPI document; no standalone versioning or changelog policy page.
OpenAPI 3.0.3 document covering the inference router and the management API, advertised verbatim in the docs llms.txt.
Mintlify default interactive playground with a "Try it" runner per endpoint; mounts client-side and executes against the production router.
The in-app Playground sends real routed requests behind login, and free models are a 200-requests/day production tier; no sandbox base URL, test keys, or isolation framing anywhere in the docs.
Dated changelog covering API-affecting changes including explicit field deprecations with migration paths; /v1 path-versioned. No standalone versioning policy or back-compat window.

Unauthenticated JSON data API over package metadata with documented endpoints and an example response schema; scope carried in the excerpt: no formal API-description artifact (OpenAPI or equivalent) exists.

No version segment in the API endpoints and no API versioning or deprecation statement; every deprecation field in the response schema governs formula lifecycles, not the API surface.
